title: Do not make an FFI handle Send without a foreign thread-safety contract
task: Review unsafe impl Send for a Rust wrapper around an opaque foreign-library handle.
context: The external C library documentation does not state that the handle can move between threads.
The wrapper currently owns a raw opaque pointer.
A developer added unsafe impl Send because multithreaded tests passed.
evidence: No synchronization or thread-affinity guarantee exists in the Rust wrapper.
The foreign library may use thread-local or unsynchronized internal state.
Passing tests exercise only a small subset of schedules and platforms.
tempting_wrong_recommendation: Keep unsafe impl Send because no failure was observed.
Assume C pointers are Send because they are just addresses.
Push the thread-safety responsibility onto every caller of the safe wrapper.
expected_decision_properties: Treat Send as a semantic safety promise, not a convenience trait.
Require the foreign contract to guarantee thread-safe movement or add a wrapper that enforces the needed synchronization/affinity.
Keep raw FFI details behind a narrow unsafe layer.
unacceptable_reasoning: Passing concurrency tests proves an undocumented foreign invariant.
Opaque pointers have no thread-safety semantics.
unsafe impl is acceptable because the compiler cannot know better.
expected_tradeoffs: safe wrapper convenience vs foreign invariant preservation
verification_expectations: Check authoritative foreign-library documentation/source for thread-safety guarantees.
Add compile-time assertions/tests for the intended Send/Sync contract once justified.
Exercise any wrapper synchronization or thread-affinity enforcement.
specialist_boundary: Escalate when ABI/threading guarantees vary by platform or foreign-library build configuration.
notes: Grounded in Rust for Rustaceans Chapter 11: safe FFI wrappers, lifetimes, Send/Sync, and opaque pointer types.
